2607.22520.title: The Regression Tax: Decomposing Why Skills Help and Hurt LLM Agents
2607.22520.paper_summary: Adding procedural skills to an LLM agent is typically evaluated by average improvement in task success. However, this metric hides an important cost: skills can also make agents worse. We measure both sides by comparing agents with and without skills across nearly 6,000 runs spanning two office automation benchmarks and three model harness stacks. This allows us to distinguish two outcomes. A regression is a task solved without skills but failed after skills are added. A residual failure is a task that fails both with and without skills. We find that regressions are substantial enough that the best performing skills outperform others primarily by regressing less, not by gaining more. We identify three causes of regression: (i) skill description osmosis, a skill changes an agent's behavior simply by being present in context, even when it is never invoked; (ii) grounding displacement, a skill's prescribed procedure overrides how the agent interprets its inputs; and (iii) verification displacement, where the procedure suppresses checks the agent would otherwise perform on its outputs. Analysing persistent failures reveals the same underlying pattern. Existing skills overemphasize procedural guidance the stage least often responsible for failure while under supporting grounding and verification, the dominant sources of remaining errors. After correcting evaluation artifacts and studying traces, we find many regressions and persistent failures recoverable through better grounding and verification. Procedural skills should be evaluated by decomposing their net effect into gains and regressions, not by aggregate improvement alone. We identify three regression modes skills should avoid, and find that reliability depends more on grounding and verification than on procedural skill choice.
2607.22520.paper_summary_zh: 將程序技能添加到 LLM 代理通常是通過任務成功的平均改進來評估的。<lb/>然而，這個指標隱藏了一個重要的成本：技能也可能使代理變得更糟。<lb/>我們通過比較約 6,000 次運行中有技能和無技能的代理，跨越兩個辦公自動化基準和三個模型框架來衡量這兩方面。<lb/>這使我們能夠區分兩種結果。<lb/>回歸是指在沒有技能的情況下解決的任務，但在添加技能後失敗。<lb/>殘餘失敗是指無論有無技能都失敗的任務。<lb/>我們發現回歸的情況相當明顯，以至於表現最佳的技能主要是因為回歸較少，而不是獲得更多。<lb/>我們確定了三種回歸的原因：（i）技能描述滲透，技能僅通過在上下文中存在而改變代理的行為，即使從未被調用；<lb/>（ii）基礎位移，技能的規定程序覆蓋了代理解釋其輸入的方式；<lb/>（iii）驗證位移，程序抑制了代理本來會對其輸出進行的檢查。<lb/>分析持續失敗揭示了相同的基本模式。<lb/>現有技能過度強調程序指導，而這一階段最少負責失敗，同時對基礎和驗證的支持不足，這是剩餘錯誤的主要來源。<lb/>在糾正評估工件和研究痕跡後，我們發現許多回歸和持續失敗可以通過更好的基礎和驗證來恢復。<lb/>程序技能應通過將其淨效果分解為增益和回歸來評估，而不是僅僅通過總體改進。<lb/>我們確定了技能應避免的三種回歸模式，並發現可靠性更多依賴於基礎和驗證，而不是程序技能的選擇。
